```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is a paying customer within 90 days, not a durable business. A's sourced evidence shows that bar is reachable. Bulletin lists live App Store pricing ($3.99/mo, $19.99/yr, $39.99 lifetime), so the monetization path exists and can take a first payment without a sales cycle.",
    "B has a sourced structural blocker that conflicts with the timeline. Handling PHI means signing BAAs, completing a risk assessment and running audited infrastructure from day one. The brief's cited estimate puts year-one HIPAA compliance at $8,000-$25,000. A solo operator would need this in place before any therapist could legally pay and use the product.",
    "B's own demand evidence undercuts the idea. The brief says the sourced complaints are about incumbent pricing and group-practice friction, not about a missing notes+reminders tool. It also says switching interest flows toward other full EHRs, not stripped-down tools.",
    "B's main sourced acquisition channel has a $500/mo minimum (Capterra PPC). The free alternative, r/therapists, has self-promotion limits. A's channels (ASO, Product Hunt, r/SideProject) cost $0 in cash. Paid UA at roughly $3.60 iOS CPI is also available in small, controllable amounts.",
    "A's strongest counter-evidence is Artifact's shutdown and the saturated, free-heavy category. Both are serious threats to scale and retention. They do not rule out a few early subscribers, and A's regulatory exposure is limited to a one-time IP consult rather than ongoing compliance."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand signal: a handful of Reddit anecdotes and a competitor's (oasys.health) aggregated reviews saying SimplePractice is 'overkill' and 'expensive.' None shows demand for a minimal notes+reminders product, and the brief admits switchers go to other full EHRs. The supporting claim about a $29 SimplePractice Starter tier cites unnamed 'third-party sources,' and TheraSoft/TheraFocus pricing has no URLs, so both count as unsourced.",
  "confidence_note": "Low-to-moderate confidence. A's evidence is also thin. Its demand rests on one Play Store review and one Reddit builder's personal pain. The claim that Bulletin, KhanList, Content Bite and Syft are single-developer apps 'already monetizing' is unsourced. Its own case against (Artifact, free clones, platform absorption) makes long-term viability doubtful. A wins mainly because B's sourced HIPAA burden and misaligned demand evidence make a first paid customer within 90 days less plausible. B has the stronger payer (businesses paying $29-69/mo), so with a longer horizon or an existing compliance setup the verdict could flip."
}
```
